Change in foot traffic relative to a baseline year

Source: R/change_index.R
change_index.Rd

Works out the average number of pedestrians per day at each chosen sensor in each year, then compares each year with a baseline year. An index of 100 means the same daily traffic as the baseline year. An index of 60 means 40% fewer people. By default the baseline is the earliest year in the data, so the index shows how foot traffic has grown or shrunk since then.

Usage

change_index(sensors, baseline_year = NULL, years = NULL, data = ped_hourly)

Arguments

sensors

Integer vector of sensor location_id values to keep. See ped_sensors.

baseline_year

The year to compare against. The default, NULL, uses the earliest year in data.

years

Optional integer vector of years to return. The default, NULL, returns every year available.

data

A data frame with the same columns as ped_hourly. Defaults to ped_hourly.

Value

A data frame with one row per sensor and year, containing location_id, sensor_name, year, daily_mean (average pedestrians per day), baseline (average per day in the baseline year) and index (daily_mean as a percentage of baseline). baseline and index are NA for sensors with no complete data in the baseline year.

Details

The average daily count adds up the 24 hourly averages for weekdays and for weekends, then weights them 5 to 2 to represent a typical week. A sensor and year are only included when both day types have all 24 hours recorded, so years with large gaps in the data are left out rather than understated.

Examples

some_sensors <- unique(ped_hourly$location_id)[1:3]
change_index(sensors = some_sensors)
#> # A tibble: 6 × 6
#>   location_id sensor_name  year daily_mean baseline index
#>         <int> <chr>       <int>      <dbl>    <dbl> <dbl>
#> 1         108 261Will_T    2025     11264.   11264. 100  
#> 2         108 261Will_T    2026     11178.   11264.  99.2
#> 3         107 280Will_T    2025      3801.    3801. 100  
#> 4         107 280Will_T    2026      3712.    3801.  97.6
#> 5         141 474Fl_T      2025      4314.    4314. 100  
#> 6         141 474Fl_T      2026      4787.    4314. 111.
